title: Source Evaluation
intent: formative · Research & Retrieval (Doing) · click through the process
statement: Apply a framework to decide whether a source is trustworthy enough to cite — before you rely on it.

steps.title: Identify the source
steps.text: See what you are dealing with: who, where, when, and what kind of thing it is.

steps.title: Check currency and authority
steps.text: Is it recent enough for the topic, and does the author have credible standing?

steps.title: Test accuracy and evidence
steps.text: Can the claims be checked? Look for citations, data and corroboration.

steps.title: Read the purpose and bias
steps.text: Ask why it was made — to inform, or to persuade and sell. Motive shapes content.

steps.title: Reach a verdict
steps.text: Weigh the lenses together: relevant is not the same as reliable.

feedForward.text: Pick one source and run it through a full framework — try the worked CRAAP, RADAR and ROBOT activities to see the same source three ways.
